rationale: The Court is most likely to issue a narrow, Roberts-assigned opinion holding that Oklahoma’s charter scheme makes charter operators state actors (Brentwood/public-function/entwinement), so the State may require nonsectarian operation without triggering Carson/Zelman equal-access rules. Thomas likely dissents on state-action grounds (Rendell-Baker/anti-labeling), with some risk of concurrences from Alito/Gorsuch/Barrett/Kavanaugh to cabin the holding and clarify Free Exercise implications.
